qa.name: Brachioradialis
qa.origin: Lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus
qa.insertion: Lateral surface of the distal radius just proximal to the styloid process
qa.function: Flexion of the elbow, especially when the forearm is in a neutral (semi-pronated) position
qa.clinical_note: Anomalous muscle — lies in the posterior compartment but acts as an elbow flexor; innervated by the radial nerve making it the only elbow flexor spared in musculocutaneous nerve injury

qa.name: Extensor Carpi Radialis Longus
qa.origin: Lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus
qa.insertion: Dorsal surface of the base of the second metacarpal
qa.function: Extension and radial deviation of the wrist
qa.clinical_note: Along with ECRB it is the primary wrist extensor — both tendons run together in the second extensor compartment at the wrist

qa.name: Extensor Carpi Radialis Brevis
qa.origin: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus via the common extensor tendon
qa.insertion: Dorsal surface of the base of the third metacarpal
qa.innervation: Deep branch of the radial nerve (posterior interosseous nerve)
qa.function: Extension and radial deviation of the wrist
qa.clinical_note: Its origin at the lateral epicondyle is the primary site of lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow) — pain reproduced by resisted wrist extension

qa.name: Extensor Digitorum
qa.origin: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus via the common extensor tendon
qa.insertion: Extensor expansions of the second through fifth digits
qa.innervation: Posterior interosseous nerve (deep branch of the radial nerve)
qa.function: Extension of the metacarpophalangeal joints of the second through fifth digits, extension of the wrist
qa.opposing_muscle: Flexor Digitorum Superficialis, Flexor Digitorum Profundus
qa.clinical_note: Inserts via the extensor expansion — complete finger extension at all joints requires cooperation of the intrinsic muscles through the same expansion

qa.name: Extensor Digiti Minimi
qa.origin: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus via the common extensor tendon
qa.insertion: Extensor expansion of the fifth digit
qa.innervation: Posterior interosseous nerve (deep branch of the radial nerve)
qa.function: Extension of the metacarpophalangeal joint of the little finger
qa.clinical_note: Allows independent extension of the little finger — its tendon runs in its own sixth extensor compartment at the wrist

qa.name: Extensor Carpi Ulnaris
qa.origin: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus via common extensor tendon, posterior border of the ulna
qa.innervation: Posterior interosseous nerve (deep branch of the radial nerve)
qa.function: Extension and ulnar deviation of the wrist
qa.clinical_note: Works with flexor carpi ulnaris to produce pure ulnar deviation — its tendon is stabilized at the distal ulna by a separate subsheath that can tear causing painful snapping at the wrist
